baseline_preserved.note: Follow-up runs use after/original and after/named directories; the baseline report and its existing artifacts were not rewritten.

changes.effect: ingest omits the position field when unresolved, allowing automatic per-source positions inside one atomic named batch. Identical old named retries resolve to their original positions. Exported/returned Documents still carry integer positions. ingest_many continues snapshotting mutable payloads before producers resume.

changes.change: Database.preview(payload) returns a list of {key,value} emissions
changes.effect: Runs only the one-document map contract. No append, identity allocation, reducer calls, cache writes, or sequence changes. Stage and preview share map response shape, cardinality, contribution limit, and JSON validation. Empty emissions expose ignored payloads before import.

Native cursor-validation errors preserve original messages and append fresh-snapshot recovery. Native/Python count bounds and ABI request-size failures suggest smaller batches or ingest_many with a smaller batch_size.

changes.change: Catalogue example covers the actual offline application flow
changes.effect: Demonstrates separate delivery/product IDs, named atomic batches with omitted positions, old creation retries after revisions, preview of supplier name/title mismatch, and empty versus absent categories.

compatibility_review.issue_caught: The initial shared helper canonicalized emitted values; this could change custom reducer inputs such as -0.0 into 0 and make reconstruction differ from an existing cache.
compatibility_review.resolution: Removed emission encode/parse roundtrips. Shared helper validates and projects raw cloned key/value fields, preserving old reducer input semantics. Only preview applies existing large-number JSON wire normalization to its response; emitted signed zero survives.
compatibility_review.regression: native/engine/tests/ux.rs includes a custom Wasm reducer that traps unless the map-emitted -0.0 reaches its input with a minus sign.

findings_followup.evidence: Named variant previews all nine valid events with one emission each and a name-only supplier payload with zero emissions. State remains unchanged.
findings_followup.remaining_limit: Callers must opt into preview or application schema validation; normal ingestion still accepts zero-emission facts by design. Preview cannot validate reducer success or prove a complete batch fits.

findings_followup.evidence: The named variant imports the same nine events in two atomic batches without supplying positions. Retrying the five-event creation batch inserts nothing, and all exported positions match the per-source sequence 0..8.
examples/catalogue.py uses outer delivery-N IDs alongside payload product a/b/mug IDs and retries the original creation batch after a revision.
examples/catalogue.py asserts a zero-count gear row after last-item withdrawal, no missing-category row, and a current-catalogue filter for zero-count groups.

comparison.sequence_note: Sequence 18 versus 15 is expected: each changed group receives one history record per batch. Grouping lifecycle observations coalesces per-category updates in the named variant. Domain outputs and retained facts match; cursors/sequences are database-local.
comparison.performance_claims: No throughput measurement or speed claim; batch counts are directly observed.

outcome.summary: The original application remains compatible. Named atomic imports remove the manual-position requirement; preview exposes malformed supplier shapes before writing. Rebuild and duplicate semantics remain correct, and custom reducer contribution inputs retain their previous semantics.
